title: B2B and Professional Services — Share of ADA Web Accessibility Lawsuits
description: Industry breakdown of ADA web accessibility lawsuits, with specific focus on B2B and professional services sectors. Data from UsableNet 2025 annual report and EcomBack 2025 annual report.

overall_industry_distribution_2025.source: EcomBack 2025 Annual ADA Website Accessibility Lawsuit Report
overall_industry_distribution_2025.note: Top 9 industries = 91.51% of all 3,948 federal+state lawsuits in 2025

healthcare_specific.trend: Rising — HHS Section 504 May 2024 final rule has not yet produced enforcement spike but is driving compliance awareness
healthcare_specific.hhs_section_504_note: HHS Section 504 final rule published May 9, 2024; took effect July 8, 2024. Compliance deadlines extended: 15+ employee organizations must comply by May 11, 2027; <15 employees by May 10, 2028. HOWEVER: underlying Section 504 obligation has been enforceable since July 8, 2024 — private right of action available now.

financial_services_specific.status: Notable 2024 uptick in both demand letters and filed cases
financial_services_specific.pct_of_total: <2% (estimated; most resolve via demand letter before court filing)
financial_services_specific.sec_nexus: October 2022 SEC mutual fund rules explicitly require ADA accessibility compliance

professional_services_b2b.note: Professional services (law firms, accounting firms, consulting, staffing, real estate B2B, insurance brokers) represent a very small fraction (<1%) of current filed cases — NOT because they are not sued, but because most cases resolve via demand letter before court filing.
professional_services_b2b.demand_letter_estimate: Most B2B professional services cases settle for $5,000–$20,000 via demand letter with no public court record
key_risk_factors: ADA Title III covers 'offices of accountants or lawyers' explicitly as places of public accommodation
B2B firms are increasingly targeted as plaintiff law firms expand beyond retail
40% of 2025 federal ADA Title III filings are now pro se plaintiffs (AI-assisted) — lowering barrier to targeting any business
Small professional services firms are preferred targets: less legal firepower, more likely to settle quickly

key_insights: Healthcare is the fastest-growing B2B/professional services sector for ADA web accessibility enforcement (2.5–3% in 2025, up from <1% in 2020)
HHS Section 504 (July 2024) creates a parallel enforcement track for all HHS-funded providers — higher stakes than private ADA lawsuits (OCR can terminate federal funding)
Financial services lawsuits are predominantly resolved via demand letter before court filing — actual exposure is higher than public court data suggests
Professional services (accounting, legal, consulting) are explicitly listed as ADA Title III 'public accommodations' but rarely appear in public lawsuit databases — demand letters dominate
The AICPA/NASBA CPA exam case (2019) shows even professional certification bodies are not exempt
Enterprise healthcare systems face the highest financial exposure: UNC Health ($125K + enterprise remediation), MedStar ($440K), Springfield Clinic (full patient portal overhaul)
